question: Does native Codex goal improve useful continuation or outcomes enough to justify enabling it in the current unified Phase 2 setup?
baseline: r26/r27 Knowledge Work control, unchanged business inputs
intervention: Native goal feature as a bundle: initial thread/goal/set, goal instructions/tools, native automatic continuation and registered two-idle-turn progress guard. Off retains ordinary turns and genuine new-state notifications, without a replacement persistence prompt. This does not isolate goal wording from its continuation mechanism.
primary_outcomes: unsupported processing entries and operations delay
prematurely stopped work that remained executable
useful post-goal continuation: new verification, action or explicit correction
secondary_outcomes: authored messages and exact peer reads
explicit method adoption after a read
shared false prerequisite with independent disproof
repeated tool calls with identical arguments and results
native continuation count and guard pauses
native observed response groups, recorded token usage and elapsed time
analysis: Compare both repetitions within each model. Preserve all outcomes, interventions, partial completions and errors; inspect complete native histories and independent replays. A small exploratory comparison informs the default for this setup, not a population rate, cross-domain necessity or a statistically established effect. Existing positive cases remain intact and are not pooled into the new paired-rollout count.
decision: Enable goal by default only if it supplies useful progress/corrections or prevents premature stopping at acceptable extra cost; retain off as a supported explicit condition. Report ambiguous or model-dependent effects without a universal recommendation.
no_optional_stopping: Finish the eight registered rollouts; do not add or replace runs because of their outcomes.
clarification: Launch order was counterbalanced, not randomized; the original frozen design and its wording remain in the evidence archive.
